summary: git push uploads your commits to a remote. git pull downloads commits other people pushed and merges them into your branch.
notes: git pull is git fetch followed by git merge. git fetch alone downloads without changing your files.
"Your branch is up to date" only means up to date with the last fetch. Run git pull to check for new work.
The pull made a merge commit because both Maya and Jordan had new commits.
pitfall: git push fails with "rejected ... (fetch first)" when someone pushed before you. Run git pull, fix any conflicts, then push again.
setup_note: Starts in Maya's clone of ../gradebook.git. Her teammate Jordan has his own clone in ../jordan and already pushed a commit Maya does not have.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add how to run"
